rounds.text: Bazel International Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.31x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.29x [E2, E7]. This valuation gap is underscored by a discounted cash flow analysis suggesting an intrinsic value of Rs 41 per share, providing a 46% margin of safety against the current market price of Rs 22 [E31, E32]. The company has demonstrated a strong long-term track record, achieving compounded profit growth of 30% over the last decade and a 31% increase in the trailing twelve months [E16, E17]. Furthermore, the business is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17x and maintains comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 2.55x [E26, E27]. A notable increase in capital work in progress of 98.4% suggests that the company is currently in a growth-oriented capex build-up phase [E28]. Conceded: the company faces challenges including a negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.28 Cr [E24], a low return on equity of 1.2% [E13], and a lack of dividend payments [E4, E38].
